note: Topical dissociated GR agonists (mapracorat/BOL-303242-X, Bausch & Lomb; AL-38583, Alcon) were carried by rabbit, guinea-pig and ocular-cell models promising steroid-equal anti-inflammatory efficacy without the IOP rise; Bausch terminated mapracorat in Q4 2013 'resulting from analysis of Phase 3 study results' (Valeant FY2013 10-K) and its patient data surfaced only as 2020 registry postings; the atopic-eczema arm of the same compound is a separate entry.
label: Allergic conjunctivitis (ocular SEGRA)

engagement.model: Primary human ocular cells (conjunctival fibroblasts, corneal epithelium)
engagement.note: Mapracorat blocked LPS/IL-1β cytokine release in primary human conjunctival and corneal cells at low-nM potency, matching dexamethasone; never read out in patients.
engagement.short: Steroid-equal cytokine block in human eye cells
engagement.quote: BOL-303242-X acts as a potent anti-inflammatory agent in various primary human ocular cells with similar activity and potency compared to classical steroids.
engagement.judgement: Mol Vis (2009;15:2606-16) carries no DOI, so the PMC URL is used. The only patient engagement trial planned for the class, Alcon's AL-38583 tear-eosinophil count after conjunctival allergen challenge (NCT00881673), was withdrawn in 2009 by 'management decision' with 0 enrolled; Cavet 2013 (PMC3716413) extended the same cell prediction to IL-4/IL-13-driven conjunctival chemokines. No tear or conjunctival biomarker was ever reported for mapracorat or AL-38583 in people.

dose.model: Rabbit and monkey topical ocular pharmacokinetics
dose.note: Rabbit/monkey PK showed 3% mapracorat matching dexamethasone tissue levels with lower systemic exposure, predicting once-daily dosing; no patient ocular exposure was ever published.
dose.quote: The favorable pharmacokinetic profile of mapracorat supports further clinical investigation and suggests that a convenient daily dosing regimen may be efficacious for this novel ophthalmic anti-inflammatory therapy.
dose.judgement: The Phase 2 post-cataract dose-ranging record (NCT00905450, results first posted 2020-09-03) shows once-daily 2-3% clearing anterior-chamber cells in 68-71% of patients vs 70-78% for four-times-daily, directionally consistent with the once-daily prediction, but no exposure or occupancy was measured in any trial and the record carries no quotable comparison, so the cell stays untested. Phase 3 went forward at 3%.

efficacy.model: Guinea-pig ovalbumin allergic conjunctivitis (rabbit paracentesis for post-surgical inflammation)
efficacy.note: Guinea-pig allergic conjunctivitis and rabbit paracentesis models put mapracorat equal to dexamethasone on clinical signs, eosinophils and aqueous protein.
efficacy.short: Equal to dexamethasone in guinea pig, rabbit
efficacy.quote: In the guinea pig, mapracorat or dexamethasone eye drops induced an analogous reduction in clinical symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis and conjunctival eosinophil accumulation.
efficacy.judgement: Mol Vis (2011;17:3208-23) has no DOI. The sponsor's own in-vivo paper, Shafiee 2011 (doi:10.1167/iovs.10-5598, abstract read), covers rabbit dry eye and paracentesis rather than allergy and concludes 'full anti-inflammatory efficacy (similar to DEX)'; Baiula 2014 (doi:10.2147/DDDT.S62659) repeated the guinea-pig result for the late phase. The guinea-pig model is the in-context one; the rabbit model is what the post-cataract Phase 3s rested on.

efficacy.model: Guinea-pig ovalbumin allergic conjunctivitis (rabbit paracentesis for post-surgical inflammation)
efficacy.note: CAC Phase 2: itching 1.34-2.11 vs vehicle 2.28, no dose order or statistics; Phase 3s cleared AC cells 15-20% vs 11-12% (loteprednol 31% vs 14-16%).
efficacy.short: Sub-steroid effect; program terminated on Phase 3
efficacy.quote: Ocular Itching (8 hours, 0-4 scale): 0.3% once a day 1.71; 2% once a day 1.34; 3% once a day 2.11; 0.3% twice a day 2.06; 2% twice a day 1.65; 3% twice a day 1.58; Vehicle 2.28.
efficacy.judgement: Closest call in the entry. Drug beat vehicle numerically in every arm of every trial, so a direction-only reading gives 'same'. Called contra because the models' stated prediction was steroid-equivalence ('analogous' to dexamethasone; 'similar to DEX'), and: (i) in the CAC trial (236 subjects, 2011, results first posted 2020-09-04) the best arm sat 0.94 units below vehicle on itching with no dose ordering (3% once-daily 2.11 vs vehicle 2.28), under the conventional >=1-unit CAC bar, and B&L never advanced allergic conjunctivitis beyond Phase 2; (ii) the three post-cataract Phase 3s (NCT01230125, NCT01591161, NCT01591655; 692 mapracorat patients; results first posted 2020-09-03) cleared anterior-chamber cells at day 8 in 15.5/20.0/15.8% vs 11.5/12.1/10.8%, under half the separation B&L's own loteprednol gel label reports on the identical endpoint ('31% vs. 14-16%', DailyMed setid 9a666065-d467-42b8-8ecd-0ec1de9986d5); (iii) Valeant's FY2013 10-K (filed 2014-02-28, accession 0000885590-14-000025) wrote off the $14.4M IPR&D asset 'related to the termination of the Mapracorat development program ... resulting from analysis of Phase 3 study results'. No p-values are posted anywhere, no peer-reviewed clinical paper exists, the quote is a transcription of the registry outcome table (no prose sentence exists), and the magnitude call is my juxtaposition; a reviewer who requires a stated miss should downgrade to 'same' with magnitude 'direction_only'. AL-38583's 312-patient Phase 2 vs Maxidex (NCT01001091, completed 2010-04) never posted results; Harrow filed an IND for an AL-38583 Phase 3 in 2026 (AdisInsight, later knowledge, not used). Year is 2020 because the registry posting is the first published patient data; the 10-K is not an allowed status source.

safety.note: Mapracorat induced myocilin, the steroid-IOP marker, to only 53% of dexamethasone's maximum in monkey trabecular-meshwork cells.
safety.short: Half the myocilin induction of dexamethasone
safety.quote: Maximum efficacy for BOL-303242-X was 53% of that for DEX.
safety.judgement: Epub 2009-08-20, print IOVS 51(1) January 2010; year follows print, model_first_use_year follows epub.

safety.note: Six weeks of 1% mapracorat left rabbit IOP unchanged while dexamethasone raised it; patients never had IOP posted as an outcome.
safety.short: No IOP rise in rabbits over 6 weeks
safety.quote: Finally, BOL-303242-X showed no effects on integrated IOP or body weight, whereas DEX significantly increased integrated IOP and prevented the increase of body weight observed in the vehicle-treated animals.
safety.reason: IOP prediction never tested in print
safety.judgement: The three Phase 3 adverse-event tables (14-18 days, 692 mapracorat patients) list no IOP-increase term, but NCT01230125 reports non-serious events only at a >=5% threshold and no trial posted IOP as an outcome, so a 1-3% steroid-type responder rate cannot be excluded and no sentence can be quoted; untested, not 'same'. The 14-day healthy-volunteer corneal-endothelium study (NCT01736462) posted nothing. Yorio 2020 (doi:10.1080/17469899.2020.1762488) reads the same rabbit data as 'mapracorat still increased IOP compared to vehicle treated rabbits', so even the model's prediction is contested. Shafiee read at abstract level.
